term: AI Hierarchy: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ Deep Learning ⊃ Generative AI
definition:
• **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**: Broad field of computer science creating machines capable of intelligent behaviour.
• **Machine Learning (ML)**: Systems that learn patterns from data without explicit rules.
• **Deep Learning**: ML using multi-layered artificial neural networks (e.g., Transformers, CNNs, RNNs).
• **Generative AI**: Deep learning models that generate novel text, code, audio, or images rather than solely predicting or classifying existing data.
examTip: AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) is theoretical and commercially non-existent. On the exam, eliminate options claiming commercial AGI or that NLP is a subset of ML (NLP is an AI subfield alongside ML).

definition:
• **Discriminative / Predictive AI**: Models $P(Y|X)$ to classify inputs into known labels, assign probabilities, or predict continuous numbers (e.g., fraud anomaly detection, spam classification, sentiment tagging).
• **Generative AI**: Models $P(X)$ or $P(X, Y)$ to synthesise new data distributions (drafting personalized emails, generating synthetic test datasets, summarizing reports).
examTip: If an email system categorizes incoming complaints, that is **discriminative AI**. If it generates response drafts, that is **generative AI**.

deck: Set 2: Google Cloud Generative AI Offerings
term: Gemini Enterprise (formerly Google Agentspace) & Vertex AI Platform
definition:
• **Vertex AI (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)**: Enterprise end-to-end ML and agent platform for model discovery (Model Garden), tuning, grounding, and orchestration.
• **Model Garden**: Enterprise catalog of first-party (Gemini, Imagen, Codey), open-source (Gemma, Llama, Mistral), and third-party models with one-click deployment.
• **Vertex AI Search and Conversation**: Turnkey RAG and multi-turn conversational agents with Google-quality semantic indexing.
examTip: Focus on the architectural capability rather than product renames: managed enterprise discovery and deployment happens in **Model Garden**; search over enterprise unstructured documents is powered by **Vertex AI Search**.

deck: Set 3: Techniques to Improve Model Output
term: Grounding, RAG, Prompt Design vs. Fine-Tuning
definition:
• **Prompt Engineering**: Zero-shot / few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought; fastest and lowest cost.
• **Grounding with Google Search / Enterprise Data (RAG)**: Connects model to live internet data or corporate repositories to eliminate hallucinations and cite verifiable sources.
• **Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT / LoRA) & Full Tuning**: Adapts model weights for domain-specific style, tone, or proprietary terminology when few-shot prompting context is insufficient.
examTip: When recent or real-time factual knowledge is required, choose **Grounding / RAG**, not fine-tuning (fine-tuning embeds knowledge statically and is expensive to refresh).

deck: Set 4: Business Strategy, Governance & Responsible AI
term: Google's 7 Responsible AI Principles & Decision Matrix
definition:
• **7 Principles**: Be socially beneficial; avoid creating/reinforcing unfair bias; be built and tested for safety; be accountable to people; incorporate privacy design principles; uphold high scientific standards; be made available for uses that accord with these principles.
• **Build vs. Buy Matrix**: High Impact + Low Complexity = Buy pre-built; High Impact + High Complexity = Custom build/tune justified; Low Impact + High Complexity = Avoid.
examTip: Google will NOT design AI technologies for weapons, surveillance violating human rights, or technologies causing overall harm.
